# Evidence Model

<!-- awf:edit-in-place body: your edits below are preserved across syncs; awf owns the rest -->
## Experiment specification

An evidentiary run starts from a saved specification that declares the claims under test, inputs, assumptions, variable domains, units, checks, tolerances, seeds, environment, resource limits, and expected transformations or convergence behavior. Record a specification change after seeing a candidate result; do not silently move the success boundary.

A final claim must be reproducible from committed or content-addressed inputs in a clean process. Interactive scratch state may help create the specification but is not an input to the final run.

## Verdicts

Every run returns exactly one verdict:

- `pass`: all required checks completed and met their declared acceptance rules.
- `fail`: at least one required check completed and disproved or violated the claim.
- `inconclusive`: execution completed but uncertainty, noise, coverage, or method limits prevent pass or fail.
- `error`: the experiment could not complete as specified.

A warning cannot silently weaken a required check. An unsupported check, unstable benchmark, undecidable symbolic result, or insufficient sample belongs in `inconclusive` unless execution itself failed.

## Result envelope

Every serious tool emits the same versioned envelope with a run ID, verdict, claims tested, measurements, uncertainty, counterexamples, environment fingerprint, artifact references, and warnings. Tool-specific measurements live inside that envelope rather than changing its top-level meaning.

Every reported numerical claim cites its run ID. Reports separate observed measurements from interpretation and retain minimized failing examples or the exact failing seeds when available.

## Acceptable evidence

A correctness claim requires at least one declared check capable of falsifying it, such as comparison with an independent reference, an invariant, a convergence study, a metamorphic property, a constraint counterexample search, a rigorous enclosure, or a checked formal proof. Agreement between two paths that share the same critical logic is not independent evidence.

A performance claim requires repeated comparable measurements of baseline and candidate in the same declared environment. Report uncertainty and setup effects separately from steady state. A result whose uncertainty covers the claimed improvement is inconclusive.

## Environment and confinement

The environment fingerprint records source revision, dirty-state identity, specification and input hashes, dependency-lock identity, compiler and flags, hardware, operating system and kernel, concurrency and affinity, relevant environment variables, and random seeds.

Runs enforce wall-time, memory, process, and output limits; disable network access by default; write only to declared temporary and artifact locations; expose accelerators only when requested; and support cancellation. A user-level installation may provide binaries or defaults, but a project run records and resolves the effective project-local configuration so evidence does not depend on hidden global state.
